body:
Second read of head `a4fbc0a47` (read-only Opus agent, nothing built). This comment is not the review. The review of mkinney on this head stands.

**Result: no blocker.**

- **What runs on the worker.** `eye_boot::spawn` gets `device.clone()`: a handle to the one device that the UI thread made. `StockEye::new` makes shader modules, pipelines, a uniform buffer and bind groups. It makes no instance, no adapter and no device. The hypothesis of #3589 (two or more instances or devices at the same time) does not apply.
- **Two threads on one device.** For about 430 ms the worker makes pipelines while the UI thread draws the first frames. wgpu 30 permits this (`Device` is `Send + Sync`; error scopes are for each thread). This was not tested on WARP or GL.
- **Failure paths.** A failed spawn builds the eye on the UI thread as before. A worker that ends without a result gives one named error. The poll is `try_recv`, one time for each frame. No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` is outside tests.
- **Until the eye arrives** the viewport draws the plain stock sheet, the same path as a device that refuses the eye. The post gate and the collision checks do not read the eye.
- **Merge.** `git merge-tree` with main is clean.

Notes, none is a blocker:

1. The worker thread is detached. If the process exits while the worker is in the shader compiler of the driver, a fault at exit is possible. The PR body lists this case as not exercised.
2. `shell_window.rs` goes from 397 to 404 lines, and `frame.rs` from 425 to 436. A split is a `P7` follow-up.
3. No test covers the path from the spawn to the first draw with the eye.

The merge waits for two things: main is red (#3602), and the trial merge on the current main has to run (`camcraft-ui` lib, the integration suites, clippy).

Maintainer decision (owner's standing word 2026-11-22: choose recommended while he sleeps).

**Held: concurrent device use in the app while #3589 is open. This PR merges after #3589 is resolved.**

- Option 1 (taken, recommended): hold the merge. This PR puts two threads on one wgpu device in the shipped app for about 430 ms at the start. That use was not tested on WARP or GL. #3589 is an open `P2` GPU fault whose cause is not known. The hold ends when the reporter of #3589 names the module that faults, or when the test lock of #3589 is verified on his machine.
- Option 2 (dropped): merge now on the clean review and the clean second read.

This is not a request for rework. The review and its label stay as they are. No change to the PR is necessary now.

An update for the hold. The lock fix for #3589 is merged, and I ran the check you asked for: 0 of 20 runs of `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` on `main` at `f35202134` ended with 0xc0000005. Details: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/3589#issuecomment-7091105228.

I also tested the start-up of this pull request. I started a release build of this branch (a4fbc0a47) and a release build of plain `main` (4c0a157e1) 50 times each on two backends, with a shipped example project: the WARP adapter ("Microsoft Basic Render Driver" through dx12) and GL (on this machine GL uses the Intel Arc B390, not a software adapter). In all 200 launches the window started, showed the project, answered, and exited with code 0. No log has a panic or a "stock eye:" message, and the Application event log has no crash event.

Limits:
- This proves nothing about the crash of #3589. A start-up uses one instance and one device.
- The launches ran on a hidden Windows desktop, so no frames were presented. On WARP both builds waited about 1 second for the first surface.
- I closed each window about 0.6 seconds after it showed the project. The eye build may still have been running in some runs.
- I could not see the eye. The only evidence is that the logs show no refusal.
- Not tested: the Intel adapter through dx12 or Vulkan, and other platforms.
- 0 failures in 50 launches excludes only a crash rate above about 6% for each build and backend.

Does this lift the hold?

Route note: the merge route is the coordinator's. Another session of this account merged this PR (`530dc11f8`) with no trial merge here. The hold of 2026-11-23 had this end condition: the reporter of #3589 names the module that faults, or the test lock of #3589 is verified on his machine. The second is met: 0 of 20 runs of the ui lib tests end with `0xc0000005` on `main` at `f35202134` (#3589, comment of 03:53Z). So the merge agrees with the recorded decision. A tip check of `main` at `4dba7019d` runs here (two ui lib runs, the shell and start-up binaries), and the post-merge run of the merge commit is the check of the tip.
